reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
join filtered results instead of filtering in joins
filter early in CTEs to reduce join data

reached_sql:
WITH pair_set AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_sk, d.d_date_sk, d.d_year, i.i_brand_id, i.i_brand
    FROM item i
    JOIN date_dim d ON i.i_manufact_id = 816 AND d.d_moy = 11
)
SELECT p.d_year, p.i_brand_id AS brand_id, p.i_brand AS brand, SUM(ss.ss_sales_price) AS sum_agg
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN pair_set p ON ss.ss_item_sk = p.i_item_sk AND ss.ss_sold_date_sk = p.d_date_sk
GROUP BY p.d_year, p.i_brand_id, p.i_brand
ORDER BY p.d_year, sum_agg DESC, p.i_brand_id
LIMIT 100
reasoning_trace:
1. COMPOSITE KEY SEMI-JOIN — TARGET: store_sales.(ss_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk) — TRANSFORMATION: Build a compact pair-set of valid (i_item_sk, d_date_sk) combinations from item.i_manufact_id=816 and date_dim.d_moy=11, then probe store_sales once on that composite key so rows failing either dimension predicate are discarded before any aggregation.

2. DENORMALIZED PAIR-SET — TARGET: item.i_brand_id, item.i_brand, date_dim.d_year — TRANSFORMATION: Carry these final grouping columns inside the same pair-set, so the surviving fact rows are already annotated with brand and year and no subsequent dimension lookups are needed.

3. DIRECT FINAL AGGREGATION — TARGET: surviving store_sales rows grouped by d_year, i_brand_id, i_brand — TRANSFORMATION: Apply SUM(ss_sales_price) directly to the filtered, annotated rows using only the final group keys, avoiding any second scan or join of store_sales.

4. TOP-N AFTER GROUPING — TARGET: ORDER BY d_year, sum_agg DESC, brand_id LIMIT 100 — TRANSFORMATION: Sort and limit only the small grouped output, never any store_sales-level intermediate result.
